text:
anya: FYI, noticed a 12-18% p99 latency regression on TP INT8 rollout from last night. Root looks like NVLink saturation + all-reduce stalls when kv cache prefetch kicks in.
kevin: ugh. is this on the new kernel-selection path or the fallback?
maria: shows up only on 8xA100 config with TP=2, PP=1. Not on 4-gpu.
anya: kernel-selection chose int8-optimized matmul kernels (fast on compute) but they increase peak memcpy bursts. Timeline shows back-to-back allreduce windows.
jamal: can you paste the perf trace snippet?
anya: here - trimmed Flame graph: 
```
compute_0  |███████----| 30ms
allreduce  |---████████| 18ms (NVLink)
memcpy     |--██████---| 12ms
idle       |---| 5ms
```
kevin: NVLink goes from 40->95% during those bursts. That explains queuing on the next kernel launch.
maria: batching heuristic also increased effective seq_len from 64->92 for some shards because kv prefetch concatenated short prefixes. So bigger matmuls more memcpy.
diana: could we change prefetch to async+throttle? Instead of prefetch full KV for all requests at once, do gated prefetch per shard.
jamal: also saw INT8 scale factors diverging on TP partition boundary. Some layers get underflow and produce noisy activations so we do extra kelvin rescale steps that add kernels.
kevin: is that FP8-specific or Int8? you said int8 rollouts.
jamal: primarily INT8, but FP8 can hit similar if the scaling strategy is global vs per-tensor. We have one global scale for matmul in kernel-selection right now.
anya: perf-bot capture shows extra re-scale calls: +4 kernels per forward that weren't present in fp16 path.
perf-bot: [%summary] regression_detected: true; p99_increase: 15%; top_causes: [nvlink_saturation, extra_rescale_kernels, kv_prefetch_burst]. Trace_id: 2073456789-xyz
kevin: quick mitigation ideas: 1) force fp16 for layers crossing TP boundary 2) gate kv prefetch to keep per-shard memcpy below X MB/s 3) add small delay between allreduce windows to allow overlap.
maria: adding delay might reduce throughput. We need better comm/compute overlap: schedule overlap windows to align with async memcpy completion. Also kernel selector could pick a slightly smaller matmul tiling that lowers memcpy peaks at small compute cost.
diana: agree. We should add a metric in console for "nvlink_utilization_by_shard" and "memcpy_peak_burst" so dedicated customers can see this.
jamal: long term: change quantization path to per-sublayer scale and bias-correct post-int8, that reduces extra rescale kernels. Also update TP partitioning to avoid hot boundaries.
anya?: (typo)
anya: action items:
- kevin: prototype kernel selector heuristic to prefer lower memcpy peak matmul for TP boundary layers — due EOD tomorrow
- diana: add nvlink/memcpy metrics to console perf pipeline — due EOW
- jamal: run INT8 scaling experiment with per-sublayer scales and post-correction on 8xA100 — due in 3 days
- maria: patch kv prefetch to async gated mode and run perf baseline — due 48h
kevin: will also add a temporary rollout flag to revert to fp16 for affected model variants.
anya: logging: if anyone adds traces, include key labels: model, tp, pp, shard_id, kv_prefetch_bytes.
diana: noted. I'll add labels to the perf trace exporter.
kevin: thanks — let's sync in the 10:30 triage. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maria: if we get a quick microbenchmark, we can try kernel-tile / memcpy tradeoff sweep tomorrow morning.
perf-bot: [task_update] tickets created: RWDT-1189 (kernel-selector), RWDT-1190 (kv-prefetch), RWDT-1191 (int8-scaling).
anya: cool. if anyone sees different hardware behavior (NVLink vs NCCL over PCIe) call it out. This looks NVLink-specific for now.
kevin: FYI I repro locally with 8xA100 on dev rig and recorded the timeline. Sharing link: https://perf/reports/2073456789
jamal: great, will run int8 debug build with extra logging.
anya: thanks all. short thread but actionable. :thumbsup:
